name: Bernoulli expected value
intuition: The long-run proportion of ones equals p.
relatedLearningOutcome: Distinguish and apply common discrete and continuous probability distributions.

name: Bernoulli variance
intuition: Uncertainty is zero at p=0 or 1 and greatest at p=0.5.
relatedLearningOutcome: Distinguish and apply common discrete and continuous probability distributions.

name: Binomial probability
intuition: Counts every ordering of x successes and weights each ordering.
relatedLearningOutcome: Distinguish and apply common discrete and continuous probability distributions.

name: Binomial expected value
intuition: Adds the expected p from each of n trials.
commonMistake: Reporting p instead of a count.
relatedLearningOutcome: Distinguish and apply common discrete and continuous probability distributions.

name: Binomial variance
intuition: Independent Bernoulli variances add.
relatedLearningOutcome: Distinguish and apply common discrete and continuous probability distributions.

name: Continuous uniform expected value
intuition: Symmetry centers the distribution at the midpoint.
relatedLearningOutcome: Distinguish and apply common discrete and continuous probability distributions.

name: Continuous uniform variance
meaning: Dispersion of a continuous uniform variable.
intuition: Only interval width determines spread.
relatedLearningOutcome: Distinguish and apply common discrete and continuous probability distributions.

name: Z-score
meaning: Signed standardized distance from the mean.
intuition: Expresses unlike scales in standard-deviation units.
relatedLearningOutcome: Standardize normal variables and interpret normal and lognormal probabilities.

name: Reverse standardization
meaning: Converts a z-score back to the original scale.
intuition: Starts at the mean and moves z standard deviations.
relatedLearningOutcome: Standardize normal variables and interpret normal and lognormal probabilities.

name: Normal interval probability
intuition: Standardize each bound and subtract cumulative areas.
workedExample: For z bounds âˆ’1 and 1, probability is about .6827.
relatedLearningOutcome: Standardize normal variables and interpret normal and lognormal probabilities.

name: Lognormal transformation
expression: X = exp(Y), where Y is normal
meaning: Transforms a normal variable into a positive lognormal variable.
intuition: Exponentiation maps every real Y to a positive X.
relatedLearningOutcome: Standardize normal variables and interpret normal and lognormal probabilities.

name: One-sample Student's t statistic
meaning: Standardized sample-mean difference when Ïƒ is unknown.
intuition: Measures the mean gap in estimated standard-error units.
workedExample: A gap of 4 and SE of 2 gives t=2.
relatedLearningOutcome: explain the central limit theorem and the application of confidence intervals and sampling methodologies

name: Standard error of the sample mean
meaning: Sampling standard deviation of the sample mean.
intuition: Averaging reduces noise at the square-root rate.
relatedLearningOutcome: Explain sampling distributions, the Central Limit Theorem, standard error, and estimator properties.

name: Confidence interval with known variance
meaning: Mean interval when population standard deviation is known.
intuition: Adds and subtracts a normal critical number of standard errors.
commonMistake: Using s while claiming Ïƒ is known.
relatedLearningOutcome: Calculate and interpret confidence intervals for a population mean using Z or Student's t.

name: Confidence interval with unknown variance
meaning: Mean interval using estimated population spread.

variables.t*: t critical value with nâˆ’1 df

intuition: Heavier t tails account for uncertainty from estimating Ïƒ.
commonMistake: Using a Z cutoff for a small unknown-Ïƒ sample.
relatedLearningOutcome: Calculate and interpret confidence intervals for a population mean using Z or Student's t.

name: Margin of error
meaning: Half-width of a symmetric confidence interval.
intuition: Coverage cutoff multiplied by sampling spread determines interval reach.
commonMistake: Calling the full interval width the margin.
relatedLearningOutcome: Calculate and interpret confidence intervals for a population mean using Z or Student's t.

name: One-sample t degrees of freedom (confidence intervals)
meaning: Degrees of freedom for a one-sample mean using sample variance.
intuition: Estimating the sample mean consumes one independent deviation.
relatedLearningOutcome: Calculate and interpret confidence intervals for a population mean using Z or Student's t.
